title: UPDATE: Level 3 evacuation orders issued for grass, structure fire near southeast Salem - NewsBreak
text: (This story has been updated with additional information) A grass fire burned two structures and brought level 3 (go now) and level 2 (be set) evacuation orders across south Marion County on July 9, according to Salem Fire spokesperson Brian Carrara and the Marion County Sheriff's Office. Level 3 "Go Now" evacuation orders were issued for: Level 2 "Be Set" evacuation orders were originally issued for these roads but have been lifted. Carrara said 38 fire apparatuses responded to the fire. The fire was first reported at 15 acres but had dropped to 5-7 acres as of 4:15 p.m. An evacuation shelter was set up at Cascade High School, located 10226 Marion Rd SE in Turner. The fire was reported at about 1:50 p.m. near Gath Road SE and Barcelona Drive SE off of Turner Road, according to the sheriff's office. The area is near the former Mill Creek Correctional Facility, a minimum security prison closed in 2021. Emergency personnel will remain on the fire through the night of July 9 due to concerning overnight winds. Level 3 evacuation orders were still in place as of 8 p.m. but level 2 evacuation orders had been lifted. The sheriff's office said the agency received assistance on the brush fire from Emery & Sons Construction, Salem Fire Department, Salem Police Department, Oregon State Police, Marion County Fire District, Turner Fire District and other agencies as well as the Willamette Valley Communications Center and METCOM. Marion County Sheriff's Office spokesman Jeremy Schwab said officials believe the grass and structure fire near southeast Salem was caused by a large commercial motor vehicle that was coming onto Gath Road from Barcelona and hit some low voltage wires. The sheriff's office said in a news release the fire is under investigation. Phyllis Stelzig, 73, said she grabbed her two dogs, medication and some water before arriving at the evacuation shelter at Cascade High School. Stelzig said she smelled smoke and saw fire engines drive by her home on Turner Road before an officer came to her door and told her to evacuate. She was waiting with her two dogs, Dewey, 8, and Wally, 1.5, at Cascade High for the all clear. Jody K, who lives on Barcelona, and her two cats were also at the evacuation shelter. She said her power was out for an hour before she heard sirens and saw an officer at her driveway. The officer was going driveway to driveway informing them to leave immediately. Without power she wasn’t able to open her garage and had to leave without cat carriers or much else. Here vehicle was outside so she was able to drive away. She said she has lived in the area for 10 years and it is the first time she’s ever experienced anything like this. Matthew Barton, 28, and his partner were also at the evacuation shelter with cat Mitzy, 16. Barton was at Crawford Crossing apartments when an officer informed residents of evacuations around 3:30 p.m. Barton grabbed chargers, important documents and Mitzy before heading to Cascade High School. The couple was heading to Independence to stay with family to try and keep Mitzy more comfortable. Aircraft completed at least eight water drops on the fire as of 4:37 p.m. Schwab said the fire was dying down and crews were beginning mop up. Radio traffic reported strong winds and spot fires. The wind was continuing to push southeast. The Red Cross had arrived at the evacuation site at Cascade High School just after 4 p.m. July 9. Marion County Sheriff's Office estimated around 10 people were at the shelter. Livestock are also able to come to the evacuation site, which is located at 10226 Marion Road SE in Turner. Cascade High School is a temporary evacuation site where volunteers are offering snack and water. If the county emergency management team informs the Red Cross people will need to stay overnight they will then mobilize to become an overnight site. The fire was bumping up about a quarter mile of Turner Road moving at a moderate speed with some torching in the southeast corner, according to radio traffic. Firefighters are aiming to hold the fire east of Turner and north of Rising Lane, according to radio traffic. Three more brush rigs were requested to spread out along Turner Road to stop the fire at Turner Road, according to WatchDuty. Carrara said multiple water tenders and engines were responding. Two scooper planes were en route to drop water on the fire at 3:41 p.m., according to the Oregon Department of Forestry. Carrara said the fire was located on a farm and multiple structures were on fire. One firefighter was injured and was being transported to the hospital in stable condition to be evaluated, Carrara said. "We're working hard to contain it," he said. Schwab said deputies were going door to door in level 3 evacuation areas and "loud hailing" evacuation warnings via loudspeaker in impacted areas. The fire was sparked by downed wires after a crash involving a power pole, according to Marion County Sheriff's Office. Deputies had closed Gath Road between Turner Road and Witzel Road. Salem Police said southbound Turner Road was closed at Kuebler Boulevard and Logistics Street SE. Both lanes of Turner Road were closed at Deer Park Drive SE and Gath Road SE. Portland General Electric reported 158 customers were without power in the area because of the crash. Isabel Funk covers breaking news and public safety for the Statesman Journal. Funk can be reached at ifunk@statesmanjournal.com or on X at @isabeldfunk This article originally appeared on Salem Statesman Journal: UPDATE: Level 3 evacuation orders issued for grass, structure fire near southeast Salem
